reviews.text: An admirable introduction of the character to the DCU and an exciting film that had actual consequences. It encompasses themes of family, displacement, responsibility and culture, and it is so authentically Latino, audiences will be cracking up.
reviews.author: Nadya Martinez

reviews.text: Blue Beetle does contain glimmers of something fresh, but it also feels like too little, too late in the face of oncoming changing tide in audience tastes.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: The Blue Beetle emerges as a noble superhero, so averse to wanton violence that it’s amusing to watch him apologize to some of the villains he’s forced to defend himself against.
reviews.author: Ian Kane

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is the kind of throwback that reminds us just how far we’ve come with comic book movies... Especially when the studio behind them plays it so safe, the end result is as bland and flavorless as this.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: There's a raid on the family home by Kord's private army that's easily the most emotionally devastating scene in any 21st century DC movie (you heard me, Martha), and would stand toe-to-toe with many of Marvel's as well.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Ten years ago, Angel Manuel Soto's "Blue Beetle" would have been a hit. But it appears at the lowest point of the genre to tell basically the same story. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: The key is that family unit and the characters... I like this family. I want to see more of this family. I care about this family.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: The film could have easily been called Blue Beetle & His Amazing Family. The filmmakers are more concerned with the supporting players than the superhero they push to the background.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Practically everything related to the superhero saga is so formulaic that the dialogue track could get swapped with that of a dozen other superhero flicks and no one would know the difference. Where the film scores is in its moments dealing with family.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: If audiences still want movies as an art form a few years from now, and we end up with an inevitable wave of nostalgia for superhero films, it seems clear to me this one will be quickly reclaimed as an unsung classic of the genre.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: It’s ok for superhero stories to be fun, creative, and inviting, all things "Blue Beetle" is, suggesting that a future outing, should this film not be a oner in the new DCU, would not only be absolutely welcomed, it would shoot up to hotly-anticipated.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The adventure of the first hero in the upcoming DCU, with its blend of humor, heart, and emotion in a Latin key, has become a strong contender to rise to the podium with the best comic book adaptations of the year.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: There's a sweet, important message in here about the importance of family, but sadly it's buried in a heavily cliched superhero flick whose beats you can list off well before they happen.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: ... What distinguishes Soto's work is the emotional honesty that is present in the work of his entire cast. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is a half-baked comedy and an even more pitiful melodrama about the importance of family. It feels aimless, as if it were cut down from under the knees before it started.
reviews.author: Justine Smith

reviews.text: Blue Beetle has moments that are plentifully enjoyed, overall when the humor works, although it does so at the cost of those clichés it supposedly aims to avoid.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Burstein

reviews.text: That love that is so authentically Latino is a key element in the story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sara Heredia

reviews.text: Blue Beetle generates just enough goodwill to warrant a tepid recommendation.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is an amiable, sincere, and fitfully enjoyable piece in the superhero genre that entertains and engages in both thrills and poignancy thanks to its grounded approach and Soto’s focus on family over special effects. Recommended.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Blue Beetle’s director, Angel Manuel Soto, and screenwriter, Gareth Dunnet-Alcocer, could have concocted a family comedy with these engaging characters, eliminating the trite superhero theatrics, and they probably would have had a stronger film.
reviews.author: Tim Miller

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is charming, disposable pop entertainment. Not every film needs to be a apocalyptic spectacle.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: While the special effects are a little clunky here, the non-action scenes featuring Jaime’s funky family circle are invariably warm, inviting, and fun.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Gareth Dunnet-Alconer's screenplay has plenty of those big laughs and deserved bad-guy-comeuppances that slay in the hyped-up atmosphere of a large audience...
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: The film serves up exactly what we now wearily expect, an over-egged slice of super-powered mulch with all the standard ingredients – blurs of action; overlong fight sequences; incoherent storytelling; and, of course, plenty of blue energy bolts.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Director Angel Manuel Soto and writer Gareth Dunnet-Alcocer do their best to weave a few additional progressive elements into this basically routine production, evidently aimed at younger viewers.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: With a smaller scale and beautiful focus on character, family, and culture... a genuinely refreshing change of pace from all the bombastic, overblown superhero features... a passionate effort that might just stand as one of the best solo origin flicks.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is a good time and proves that with the right blend of heart and passion the lesser-known superheroes can soar.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: … if you’re up for two and a bit hours of amiable character work, noisy action (with dodgy CGI), good representation but a one dimensional villain and zero surprises, you might find something to like in Blue Beetle.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: Blue Beetle won’t recharge the timeline, but in taking itself less seriously it provides a sense of levity to a genre so often bogged down in its own self-importance.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: If there’s a second movie, and that’s a big if, there’s a lot in Maridueña’s performance and the celebration of “la familia” that can be built on.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: It's a great story about family... There were a couple of moments I completely forgot I was watching a superhero film. I just wanted to spend time with these people.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Arrives with low expectations, but the film is a pleasant surprise.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: For me it's a bifurcated experience with this movie. I appreciated it from a "la familia" level, but on any kind of comic book, action-adventure level, I thought it was kind of subpar.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: I had a fun time and can't begrudge a movie giving Adriana Barraza, a great Mexican actress, a lot of cheesy lines to deliver.
reviews.author: Manuel Betancourt

reviews.text: Blue Beetle hits everything we could want in a comic book adaptation and easily surpassed my expectations!
reviews.author: Sabrina Ramirez

reviews.text: Feels like something you've seen before but scrapes by thanks to the cast.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: By the time Blue Beetle’s end credits start rolling ahead of a pretty predictable mid-credits teaser, there’s a solid chance you’ll find yourself thinking that it would have been more memorable had Warner Bros. not taken so long to get it into theaters.
reviews.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore

reviews.text: The film is, in its last instance, wasted potential.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: An adventurous superhero flick with the unique combination of family drama.
reviews.author: Ganesh Aaglave

reviews.text: The best film DC has put out in a while, 'Blue Beetle' offers fun, heartfelt action and comedy. Xolo Maridueña shines as Jaime Reyes, while director Ángel Manuel Soto succeeds in delivering an ode to Latin American culture in a superhero outfit.
reviews.author: Daniel Pacheco

reviews.text: Ultimately, Blue Beetle reverts back to the tried-and-true superhero template.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Blue Beetle punches well above its weight visually; the effects are terrific and give the film a scale and spectacle the equal of any film in the genre with three times the cash available.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: While it plays like a lot of most superhero films, this still has its own unique charm and that's due to the style and culture that makes this a entertainment watch.
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: Formulaic and uninspiring family-orientated superhero DC comic book film.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: This superhero origin/adventure tale packs equal amounts of action, social commentary, family drama and Hispanic pride.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Essentially Max Steel with a budget, but its charm remains.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Mariduena’s charm keeps us hooked, while the positive message regarding the power of family is sincere and ultimately poignant. As a result, “Beetle” is able to keep superhero fatigue at bay, at least for two hours.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: This is one of the most low-key comic book films ever made. That laid back approach proves to be the film's strength, with "Beetle" one of the most charming surprises of the year.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: With an emotional family-focused core and some unique visual flourishes, it is a standout amongst recent superhero films.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: What makes Blue Beetle... more interesting than other typical superhero films is that Jaime isn’t tragic and he’s far from being alone. Despite their struggles, Jaime’s family are around him, supporting him and fighting with him from the very beginning.
reviews.author: Maan Jalal

reviews.text: A new superhero movie that never breaks away from the pack.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: A hearty caper that flies above formulaic narrative and superhero fatigue.
reviews.author: Bhuvanesh Chandar

reviews.text: The charm is undeniable to the point that it's hard to not be happy with the film by the end...yet it has many noticeable issues that ultimately hold it back from being a memorable entry to the genre. High on potential, lower on execution.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Blue Beetle has certain things going for it, even for what is ostensibly a by-numbers origins tale.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is one of the last films in the soon-to-be-defunct DC Extended Universe... It’s too late to salvage the series, but Soto deserves credit for creating one of the more charming entries in a mixed-bad franchise.
reviews.author: Daniel Rester

reviews.text: In Soto’s hands, what would become a genuinely generic superhero story becomes a swell tribute to Mexican-American culture which filters its way from the reference-heavy dialogue to the style of the fight scenes.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: There's actually this battle not just between good and evil in the movie but also a little bit of class warfare that's going on, and that feels different than [other] superhero underdog stories.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: This movie is really fun... The thing that makes this different from a lot of the big shiny noisy spectacles is that family element.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: The Reyes family are by far the best thing about this otherwise by-the-numbers caper. Funny, endearing and surprising, they recall the family in The Incredibles, and give the story its heart.
reviews.author: Dave Golder

reviews.text: At the heart of "Blue Beetle" are themes of family, community, gentrification, and corporate greed, all rolled into one unoriginal but fun flick.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: It's such a shame that this movie will probably underperform because it's actually quite a fun time. The family dynamics really works and adds some heart to the thing. Please give us more.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: A very charming superhero movie.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Too silly, too cheesy and too obvious, Blue Beetle fails to pack a powerful punch when needed, especially when highlighting issues including elitism, racism, gentrification and ignorance.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text:
BlueBeetle is enjoyable. A focus on family and Latin culture keeps the film grounded in heart. Xolo Maridueña is solid.

It can feel like a Power Rangers parody at times but a strong third act saves it. It’s a mix between the first Shazam! and Ms. Marvel.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: BLUE BEETLE is one of those films that best exemplifies Roger Ebert's quote of "it's now what a movie is about, it's how it's about it."
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Another DC Universe entry that is just too late in the rotation to stand out as anything but a simplistic rehash of old material that never fully takes advantage of the cultural relationships and surroundings that serve as the only identifying trademark.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Blue Beetle was absolutely baller! it superseded my expectations with its heartfelt story , family dynamic and well directed action!
reviews.author: Matthew Haynes

reviews.text: Blue Beetle has a distinctive creative voice that needs to be heard. The Reyes family is a wonderful addition to the cinematic comic book canon.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Submit to the fun fast-paced romp and you'll find it to be one of the more engaging movies of the summer. Its blend of fun, heart, and important representation make this one a real winner.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is both scrappy and tailored, poignant and breezily amusing. Pitched from a new angle and guided by talented hands, Blue Beetle is a rarity in these superhero end-times: a genuine pleasure to watch, reviving tired old formula with brio.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: This is an origin story for the titular character, paired with a one-off adventure. No more, no less. And all things considered, it’s not bad.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: This light-hearted, clever B-movie steeped in Latino culture is a more appealing superhero future than another Gothic Gotterdammerung.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: For a comic book superhero blockbuster, this movie has an unusual sense of peril in its action scenes, largely because it takes the time to develop its characters and their connections with each other.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: This one’s for the kids.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: With thrilling visual effects action and a touching cultural look at family, the film introduces one of the genres coolest and most relatable superheroes yet.
reviews.author: Jonathan Garcia

reviews.text: The Reyes family are the heart and soul of Blue Beetle.  George Lopez's Mexican Doc Brown, Adriana Barraza's revolutionary Nana and Susan Sarandon as a villain are fire! This film leaves the sweetest sting ever!
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: While Blue Beetle has plenty of heart and a fresh perspective, the villains and the heroes are a forgettable blend of standard comic book fare that’s never as interesting as the movie’s relaxed, warm, and loving scenes where this DC film lives.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Largely good natured and charmingly Mexican-flavored, it's also crucially lacking in coherent action set pieces. And so it's a bit like a cup full of drywall insulation covered with Tajín and Chamoy.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Gather the family for this fun-filled adventure chock-full of laughs and plenty of heart. Xolo Maridueña and George Lopez lead the solid cast which also includes the great Adriana Barraza as the scene-stealing Nana.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Worth seeing, but with many missed opportunities.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: Despite the ongoing talk about superhero fatigue setting in, Blue Beetle is very enjoyable by doing what it’s supposed to but with new, smarter approaches.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Even if it is the cinematic equivalent of microwaved leftovers, Blue Beetle is generally a good time, largely thanks to Xolo Maridueña.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: You can keep Marvel’s Avengers and DC’s Justice League. The Reyes family is the only superhero team we want right now.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: On the surface, it's entertaining to see the references to Mexican culture and enjoy a varied (and very Latino) soundtrack, but apart from that (and the solid central performances), “Blue Beetle” doesn't offer much. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: The superhero genre is a little bit crowded, and while I think I'm not sure if this is anything hugely different from the many others, it is entertaining.. It has a lot of funny moments, and the action is well choreographed.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Sometimes it’s better to keep it simple. The layup will suffice to build momentum besides the 360 Tomahawk dunk. 'Blue Beetle' provides just enough juice for a franchise seeking nourishment.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: I did not expect to cry during Blue Beetle. Twice...I was not ready for a film that not only delivers a solid superhero origin story but does so with a tremendous amount of heart and sincerity.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text:
The actors were funny and lovable, but the Blue Beetle’s real enemy in this movie was the stereotypical Hollywood trope.

I really wanted to love Blue Beetle. I really did.
reviews.author: Vincent Schilling

reviews.text: Most of the superhero elements in Blue Beetle is stuff we see on a weekly basis now. Jaime's family is full of personality and elevates the film above average.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Blue Beetle as a superhero is something that can be enjoyed by everyone in equal measure, Blue Beetle the movie is something that will especially connect with Latine audiences.
reviews.author: Lissete Lanuza Sáenz

reviews.text: it's difficult to imagine Blue Beetle becoming one of the comic book movies that is remembered a few years — or even six months — down the line.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: It’s like the movie is screaming for Blue Beetle to be a hero for La Gente (The People), but it didn’t want to lean too hard on that so as not to scare the white audience and instead, subbed in the soft-ball Shazam stuff.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: Blue Beetle features some fun action sequences, a fantastic score, and a charismatic performance from Xolo Maridueña. Susan Sarandon plays a throwaway villain, but the movie thrives when this wonderful family is on screen.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is a fun and funny film that celebrates the Latin culture in authentic ways while also delivering an engaging, thrilling & touching superhero movie! Xolo Maridueña delivers a star making turn under the confident direction of Angel Manuel Soto.
reviews.author: John Rocha

reviews.text: Blue Beetle progresses into an aggressively generic and padded-out midsection that slowly-but-surely drains the viewer’s interest and attention...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: This is, first and foremost, fun – and it wouldn’t be half as much fun were it not for the boisterous dinner-table vibe that drives the film.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: An exciting, fun, and wholesome superhero origin...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: A funny, heartfelt and culturally-significant entry into the superhero genre. With family at its center, the film’s true superheroes are the Reyes family.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Charm and personality do a lot to help this. It feels oddly dated; such a young, fresh character deserved a fresher movie.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Soto shoots all of the action clearly and knows when to end a sequence too, be it action or comedy. It’s deftly made, never wearing out its welcome, and how many superhero films can you say that about these days?
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is a hollow, uninspired recycling of superhero tropes. Every idea, both significant and inconsequential, is lifted from works that are just as formulaic and tired as it is.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: With plenty of heart and fun, DC’s Blue Beetle ushers in an exciting new hero for the big screen, and if this is a sign of things to come in DC’s new chapter, then it’s a step in the right direction.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Yes, this is but another CGI heavy superhero origin story about a young guy accidentally acquiring superpowers and awkwardly learning how to deal with them. But the refreshing spirit to be found in this young guy's family redeems the whole movie.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Blue Beetle embarks on a deeply emotional journey intricately woven with engaging family dynamics. Despite the standard superhero tropes, the movie’s charisma and sentimental depth converge to create a compelling theatrical experience.
reviews.author: Surya Komal

reviews.text: A dynamic superhero origin story about the power of family, full of references to Mexican culture and values. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: While Blue Beetle may not introduce anything novel to the comic book genre, its hero's connection to a tightly-knit, lovable Latino family stands as its greatest asset.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: This film follows the same old superhero formula. One difference is that it emotionally draws heavily on the culture of Mexican family to create the backstory of the characters’ motivation.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: It’s not some kind of comic-book masterpiece but it’s cute and the cast is likable.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The charming feeling that arrived during the dramatic moments rendered not so much as hollow but lost and frustrating.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Though it may have some novel elements, the franchise already feels tired, and isn’t much more promising than recent DC efforts “Black Adam” and “The Flash.” This beetle doesn’t have much juice.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is emblematic of what the superhero movie has become in 2023: an overlong slog through well-worn tropes.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Blue Beetle has a lot of heart and entertaining scene but it feels uninspired and dated.
reviews.author: Sarah Cook

reviews.text: Blue Beetle could’ve been a good movie, but it falls short due to its inclination towards generic superhero tropes, thereby straying away from everything that screams “Latino.”
reviews.author: Pramit Chatterjee

reviews.text: The film’s casting is excellent, beginning with Xolo Maridueña as Jaime.
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Blue Beetle tends to fare best in its smaller moments, which merely reinforces the concept’s limitations thanks in part to the sheer glut of similar fare driven by streaming.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Angel Manuel Soto's film gives space to the post-teen panic of having no clue what you're doing – shooting that feeling into the stratosphere with the responsibility of becoming a history-making superhero.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: A charming cast, distinct voice, and strong individual elements elevate Blue Beetle's fairly simple story.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: It’s got heart and some fun spectacle, but it draws from other more recognizable blockbusters that it lacks originality.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: As a stand-alone title with refreshingly low stakes and a rock-solid emotional center, it’s worth your time.
reviews.author: Kayleigh Donaldson

reviews.text: ... The Reyes family is replete with memorable characters, and the use of Spanglish and cultural clashes make of Blue Beetle the funnest superhero movie of the year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fran Chico

reviews.text: There are no surprises to be had here, no interesting twists on the superhero conventions, and no originality in even in the post-credit sequence that has the whiff of inevitability about it.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: While Blue Beetle tells a familiar story, it still manages to distinguish itself by putting the focus on the lead character's family.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: To be perfectly honest, I was never a fan of the Jaime Reyes Blue Beetle comics...Yet, something about the ads for this movie intrigued me enough to be optimistic...And, you know what? I actually enjoyed it.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is an honest and fun project that constantly does new things with a concept that could get a shaky franchise out of a lot of trouble. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is the latest blockbuster to trot out a tired old saw that turns corporate representation into a contract with the people being represented.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: The plucky Latino superhero of DC’s 'Blue Beetle' gets all suited up with nowhere to go.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: This was one of the few live-action superhero movies I genuinely enjoyed in a while without any real issues or critiques. I hope they let this continue into Film/TV continuity because it can work a great start in many people’s minds.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Dancing on the line between silly and stupid is challenging, with “Blue Beetle” frequently fumbling from the former to the latter. But are you really going to stay mad at a movie that features a climactic fight scene set to Cypress Hill? I didn’t think so
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Blue Beetle should turn things around. It features an actor who understands how such roles should be played. Toss in a fun supporting cast and the Blue Beetle can save the DC comic book movie world from a serious case of the doldrums.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Director Ángel Manuel Soto goes big on humour and heart and gets the vibe exactly right, ensuring there is plenty for adults and loads for viewers aged six to eleven.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: It may not move the genre forward in any way, but it reminds us of exactly why we loved superheroes and how their decline has left a black hole in our cinematic diet.
reviews.author: Freda Cooper

reviews.text: Blue Beetle, helmed by Ángel Manuel Soto and written by Gareth Dunnet-Alcocer, is sometimes silly and derivative but it also displays genuine heart and soul.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: It has been a while since this reviewer has seen a movie that wants to be liked so desperately.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: I just feel like I've seen this movie before.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: DC have an uncanny knack for conjuring ugly CGI, and while the effects here are not as ghastly as they were in, say, The Flash, Blue Beetle’s climax is pretty wearing.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: There are some mildly amusing moments but I’m not sure if Jaime’s eccentric uncle (George Lopez) and gun-toting granny (Adriana Barraza) freshen it up enough.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: The charms of the gritty family narrative too often clash, rather than blending in, with the science-fiction concepts and high-tech gadgetry.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: They borrow a lot  from Spider-Man, but, hey, steal from the best. The cast is a lot of fun.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Because of the family story at the heart of it [the movie] that is why this movie works, otherwise you've seen this kind of superhero movie before.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: As a super-hero origin story, “Blue Beetle” follows the well worn playbook of dozens of other movies of this type.
reviews.author: Rick Romancito

reviews.text: Xolo Maridueña is dream casting as Jaime You can feel the excitement he has for the character, and that translates with that youthful, charming presence on screen.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: The characters frequently charm... with their unabashed expressions of family devotion, including macho males who aren’t afraid to say “I love you” to each other.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The film’s greatest feat of superheroism is Xolo Maridueña’s ability to shine in spite of a script that gives him nothing but cold, stale leftovers to work with.
reviews.author: Justin Clark

reviews.text: Blue Beetle’s action sequences are clean but largely unremarkable; they work, however, because we’re into the characters.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: If DC fans are hoping for a solid, uncomplicated (no continuity knots), and most of all fun DC superhero movie that even teens and kids can enjoy –  Blue Beetle may very well be the first DC film in a decade that can deliver on all those fronts.
reviews.author: Kofi Outlaw

reviews.text: It gets pretty maddening over time. The writing leans heavily on its domestic charms yet confines its characters within a conventional copy-and-paste story. Along the way it makes several heavy-handed statements...but none of them have bite.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Heartwarming and exciting but also overstuffed and tripping over its own feet, Blue Beetle is a frequently charming, frequently frustrating attempt to re-write (or at least re-aim) the classic superhero narrative and intermittently succeeding.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: Its flaws exist in the same way they do in most of these types of movies, but a unique power set being handed over to the kinds of folks who do not often get to be seen in this sort of spotlight helps it stand out as worthwhile.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: A guy standing and screaming at his own silly outfit is neither dramatic nor visually absorbing.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: The thrills in the first Latino superhero epic are mostly generic but the personal relationships between protagonist Jaime Reyes (a charming Xolo Maridueña) and his irresistibly rowdy and resilient relatives make all the difference. Viva la familia!
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: “Blue Beetle” is a watchable time-waster made better by the actors and the cinematography by Pawel Pogorzelski.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: Aside from the jokes, there’s not much to this derivative origin story full of cliches. It feels like a cross between Venom and Spider-Man: Homecoming. There’s certainly not enough to Blue Beetle to dispel the superhero fatigue audiences are feeling.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: “Blue Beetle” works not because of its youthful, reluctant hero but despite his all-too-familiar presence. The film's real hero is the unstoppable power of family and the love that unites them.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: DC's latest, is a mostly entertaining, low-stakes romp that is a refreshing anomaly in an overstuffed genre.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: It would be a shame if this was the last outing of Blue Beetle because his adventures and stories show the potential to only get more interesting from here.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: Blue Beetle” a competent popcorn movie that adds little to the genre except some welcome inclusivity.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: This is a crowd-pleaser: entertaining, with a healthy dose of comedy, reasonably solid action set-pieces, and, most significantly, heartfelt performances. It’s just a genuinely good time at the movies
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: This is a silly action adventure family comedy that feels like it belongs more on a kid network rather than the first super hero in the new DCEU lineup.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: At a point where I’m finding superhero cinema slightly tiresome, the charms of this amiable, sweet-natured film won me over.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: As a young actor cast to portray a Latino Superhero, Maridueña is a strong choice.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: “Blue Beetle” arrives as DC is struggling to stay alive after a series of flops, cleaning house and revamping its famous comic book titles to course correct. In all the turnover, they’d be smart to keep Jaime Reyes and Xolo Maridueña around.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Lotsa fun, &  Xolo as the Blue Beetle has a lot of sincerity & star power. George Lopez manages to steal every scene he's in, and Susan Sarandon enjoys her new found villain persona. Some sticky CGI towards the end, but you can't beat the reluctant hero.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Nonetheless, the movie fails to generate emotion or tension for its two hours, since it is an exercise in genre executed with reluctance and automatism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Martina Hirsch

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is a big-energy adventure that’s made for multiple generations to enjoy, but it also reflects the corazón of its culture.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Blue Beetle makes history as the first Latino DC superhero to lead a film, but the freshness that comes along with that is overwhelmed by the usual superhero dross.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Though it doesn't stand out, strive to innovate or surprise, Blue Beetle complies in entertaining its audience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Miguel Calabria

reviews.text: Blue Beetle attempts to weave culturally specific histories of marginalization and resistance into a narrative about family legacies. But these bits come off as a weak copy of what came before, minus any emotional investment.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: A few bugs, but overall a solid DC film. This super bug has the same superhero shell, but Xolo's performance grows on you.
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: "Blue Beatle" manages to avoid a lot of cliches as it navigates a movie release schedule full of superhero fatigue. And it really comes together in the final act.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is the latest product off the superhero production line and it’s as tediously familiar as rail strikes and rainy Augusts.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: The structure follows all the tropes audiences have come to expect in a film of this type, but Maridueña IS Jaime Reyes and Blue Beetle is a serviceable launch to a hero that has big potential for James Gunn’s emerging DC cinematic rebirth.
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text: It’s tough to watch a movie that begins with a spring in its step end up in a winded heap of digital effects and explosions.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Amidst saccharine motivational phrases about the value of family, the first Latino superhero emerges. It seems difficult to find in him a genuine, deep emotion when his identity is built upon disposable materials. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: That's the secret power of Blue Beetle. The investment in Jaime as a character connects beautifully to the stakes of wanting to see the best happen for his entire family as they face crisis after crisis.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Blue Beetle isn't only the best DC movie since The Suicide Squad, but it's the best superhero movie release of the year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: For this Chicane critic, Blue Beetle is at its best when it grounds itself in real-world stakes and culture, creating a movie that feels thoughtful and lived in.
reviews.author: Alejandra Martinez

reviews.text: Blue Beetle has plenty of action and humor, but the heart of this film is in its celebration of the strength, love, and resilience of the Latino family.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: Instead of redefining a genre and imbuing it with new life via a vibrant cultural backbone, Blue Beetle only further enhances the feelings of growing superhero fatigue.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: For fans of El Chapulín Colorado, the movie may produce ecstasy, but it's also true that more is sometimes less, and the jokes and references to La Familia are almost overwhelming. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Positioning Blue Beetle as a child of migrants allows director Ángel Manuel Soto and writer Gareth Dunnet-Alcocer to make their points early and often about the side-lining and stereotyping of Mexican and Latinx culture and entertainment within the USA.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Ángel Manuel Soto plays things safe with a breezy origin story that harkens back to Sam Raimi’s original Spider-Man, with a little - but not enough - Cronenbergian body horror for good measure.
reviews.author: Lucas Hill-Paul

reviews.text: “Blue Beetle” makes it clear that the real super-powers here are a devoted family and a culture of resilience and make-do.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: In broad story-and-action terms, there really isn’t much here that feels fresh... But Blue Beetle makes one smart decision that saves its shiny cerulean ass: it brings Jaime’s family along for the ride.
reviews.author: Dan Jolin

reviews.text: Blue Beetle feels pitched at a younger audience than much superhero fare, with its candidly likeable teen-idol lead and unfussy approach.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: It’s lightweight and over-amped. Diverting but ultimately, forgettable.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: a good old-fashioned origin story, a stand-alone film unrestrained by crossovers and cameos. As a hard reset for the troubled DCEU, it’s refreshing, despite its adherence to formula.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: It’s somewhat of a disappointment, but at least “Blue Beetle” never takes itself too seriously.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: “Blue Beetle” remains both faithful to the superhero format yet gives it new life with family, culture, and humor.
reviews.author: Monica Castillo

reviews.text: Gareth Dunnet-Alococer's screenplay ... seems more eager to make checkmarks of formula than to give this hero something—anything—that sets him apart...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: While Jamie Reyes Blue Beetle isn’t as endearing as Ted Kord’s, the movie still finds its audience.
reviews.author: John Kirk

reviews.text: There’s a measure of charm, some goofy and some sentimental, infusing the domestic dynamic...[but] emerges as a rather undistinguished example of the genre, marred by a rote origins plotline, a boring villain...and mediocre CGI.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Xolo Maridueña was not only perfectly cast for the role, but he also gave a really solid performance.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: There are so few moments in 'Blue Beetle' where anything unexpected happens, but the strength of its cast helps to sustain it past this and leaves you with an experience that is something bordering on enjoyable, if forgettable.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Maridueña makes for an appealing lead, and the back-and-forth with his Blue Beetle personality (voiced by Becky G) is fun.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: …despite the aspiration to create Cronenberg for kids…Blue Beetle is typically juvenile fare…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The film's biggest strengths lie in its depiction of Latino culture & family dynamics, but it suffers from horribly uninteresting antagonists & a lack of creativity. It's entertaining enough, but George Lopez's wacky uncle is the only thing I'll remember.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: While not reinventing the genre wheel, puts heart, emotion & unapologetically Latin energy and culture, which has so many differences between countries, but united on the desire to enjoy life and protect our people. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Like Spider-Verse & the new TMNT, Blue Beetle goes harder than expected! While a lot of attention has been given to its Latino representation, which is very well done, this is also a fun superhero origin story. A potential star turn by Mariduena...
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Blue Beetle has enjoyable family dynamics and a generic superhero origin story fighting for screen time.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: If even a low-stakes, fairly derivative superhero movie like this can charm thanks to its warm Hispanic perspective and winning supporting cast, there’s plenty of hope yet for the genre -- bugs and all.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is an entertaining, buoyant, hilarious nugget of a film that will make you feel deeply, and might even make you think deeply, if you let it.
reviews.author: Teresa Jusino

reviews.text: This unremarkable story, along with cheap-looking visual effects and Soto’s colorless direction, is a prime example of somnambulist filmmaking that lulls the audience into a mindless stupor.
reviews.author: Maya Phillips

reviews.text: If Blue Beetle encourages viewers to look into the real history behind the references, it could potentially do more good than any other DC movie.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Surprisingly unexciting, Blue Beetle feels like an uninspired mashup of a dozen other superhero films.
reviews.author: Joseph Robinson

reviews.text: This is an exciting superhero introduction for those familiar with the character and for those just learning who this Blue Beetle is.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: A super charming & fun superhero origin story. Blue Beetle will leaving you wanting more from Jamie & the Reyes Family.
reviews.author: Cris Parker

reviews.text: Director Ángel Manuel Soto has crafted a highly entertaining film that lovingly spotlights the Reyes family and their Mexican American culture and allows Maridueña to shine as a hero that everyone can cheer for.
reviews.author: Ron Seoul-Oh

reviews.text: Despite a charming and funny ensemble, Latino people now have their very own generic DCEU movie
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The film is far from perfect with questionable visuals at the start, but this wholesome superhero comedy will have you cheering, laughing and crying. The three essentials needed for a great time at the movies.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: What distinguishes it from the overarching franchise’s recent outings is its ability to integrate a genuinely tender and nuanced approach to character within its genre-required thrills.
reviews.author: Travis DeShong

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is a fun and action-packed film filled with heartwarming moments, especially with the Reyes family, which is the film’s greatest strength. Though Blue Beetle succeeds in its heroes, it fails its villains by the one-dimensional Victoria Kord.
reviews.author: Laura Sirikul

reviews.text: The DC Universe gets a much-needed Latino infusion with a superhero origin story based on the importance of family. Blue Beetle breaks the comic book adaptation mold by giving a young Mexican protagonist the blockbuster popcorn cinema treatment.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: A warmed-over origins story with some contradictory messaging about violence, it plays like a weak riff on Marvel’s rival Ant-Man films, with a bit of Venom and various iterations of Spider-Man thrown in.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: For every mention of revolutionary direct action, there is a scene with a stereotypical trope, so I'm not convinced that the film takes a major step forward in terms of representation.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Whereas Jaimie may come from a different place to most heroes of superhero flicks, nothing sets the Blue Beetle itself apart from the dozens of competing magical brawlers we have endured over the past two decades.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: A scrappy, low-stakes superhero flick brimming with charm and cultural specificity, even if the exoskeleton around it is a bit too brittle for its own good.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Blue Beetle sometimes gets trapped in a familiar superhero formula, but the movie’s comedic charm, rollicking style, and authentic chemistry among the cast members are a winning combination.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The action sequences prove to be just as weak and ineffectual as the characters – fueled by unimpressive CG duels, humdrum fight choreography, and an unthinkable lack of tension.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The entertaining Blue Beetle leaves you wanting to see more of Jaime Reyes – even if it can't help suffering from familiar superhero issues.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: Blue Beetle's family-centric story has universal appeal, but the strength of the new DC movie lies in Jaime Reyes' ties to his Mexican heritage.
reviews.author: Tatiana Hullender

reviews.text: Xolo Maridueña is undoubtedly a star in the making, he was born to play Blue Beetle and knocks it out of the park with his personable and charming performance.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: An often funny and occasionally thrilling, but over-produced spectacle with dull action, clunky exposition and an uneven tone.  The charismatic, hilarious Adriana Barraza is Blue Beetle's MVP.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: The CGI and special effects aren’t always flawless and the lore could be more developed to build out the story better, but the focus on the loving bond of family makes this memorable and enjoyable.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: Ultimately, it devolves into the kind of chaotic clash of robot-suited antagonists that has become, in this era of the comic movie, demoralizingly repetitive and, dare I say it, boring.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: BLUE BEETLE simply has heart. The family focus is sweet and fun. The retro look feels charming and the soundtrack is killer. Therefore, it’s easy to forgive its few flaws.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: This heartwarming, crowd-pleasing comic book flick is less serious and more colorful than the tonally dour mood of many contemporary superhero films.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Not only does BLUE BEETLE offer great Latinx representation, but it dives deep into the values of family and community. There’s a lot of love onscreen, and it proves quite poignant.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: The family dynamic, emotional beats, performances and direction feel so authentic it'll leave you wondering why it took so long to see true Latino representation in the superhero genre.
reviews.author: Lucas Moore

reviews.text: Reyes isn't just the first DC film superhero who's Latino -- he's also the first movie superhero to show that while his physical power comes from his super-enhancements, his fortitude comes from a loving family.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Blue Beetle does a great job showcasing the vulnerability and bravery of its main character. It also boosts a strong family identity that brings laughs, tears, and an authentic connection with the story.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: Blue Beetle works, basically, and that puts it ahead of the game for most DC Comics-derived movies.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The emotional beats are strenuous yawns, the crashing lack of novelty disguised desperately, but not well. It’s dim, and it’s dull.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is a film that earns a...grito. As a story, it knows who Jaime is and leans into the character beyond his suit and powers… While some characters have just become a mantle you can change from one person to the next, Jaime Reyes is Blue Beetle.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is broad and endearingly kid-friendly in its humor. It is also precise in its homages to Mexican culture.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: The filmmakers and the SFX team have created a memorable visual style for the film, supported by a wide array of Latino talent that underpins the authenticity of the narrative and the visuals.
reviews.author: Justin Lowe

reviews.text: James Gunn's superhero slate is off to a promising start with Ángel Manuel Soto's DC adventure, which is filled with action and big heart.
reviews.author: Sabina Graves

reviews.text: While it’s great to see a Latino get center stage, this is a mostly by-the-numbers origin story with underwhelming VFX and a disappointingly cartoonish villain.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Just when you thought super-films couldn’t get any more mechanical comes Blue Beetle, the story of ‘ancient alien biotechnology’ which turns out to have heart, soul, and some serious politics.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: Blue Beetle brought a huge smile to my face. A gigantic throwback to 2000’s era filmmaking with a beautiful Latin culture mixed all into it. Come for Blue Beetle and be ready to fall in love with Xolo Maridueña & the Reyes family
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Blue Beetle brings necessary diversity to the screen...
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Not sure I’d need to see it again, or be excited for a sequel, but makes for a nice partner feature with the great Alita: Battle Angel.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: What director Angel Manuel Soto and screenwriter Gareth Dunnet-Alcocer are bringing to the screen via Reyes’ rise into the good-guy ranks isn’t just a genre, but a culture.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Stand down the undertaker: this spirited outlier shows there’s life in the old DCEU yet. Over to you, Aquaman 2.
reviews.author: Neil Smith

reviews.text: Quite simply the best DC movie in years, and should be the blueprint for James Gunn as he moves forward with the new DCU.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The DC movie universe has been holding out for a hero, and it might just be a 22-year-old Mexican college grad with a really cool family.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Blue Beetle is at its best when delivering something boldly original and heartfelt, though it’s boxed in by more than a few reductive, stereotypical superhero story beats.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: This movie’s Latin flavor feels fresh, with welcome bits of political bite and funny takes on the genre’s over-familiar conventions.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: With deep roots in Latin American culture and a tone that blends Paul Verhoeven’s Robocop with Marvel’s quip-based comedy (before it wore out its welcome), DC’s latest movie succeeds entirely on its own terms.
reviews.author: Jake Kleinman

reviews.text: While this hero might sound like a mash-up, Blue Beetle breaks the mold by celebrating Jaime's greatest strength, his family, rather than defaulting to a story about yet another brooding solo knight.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Under Ángel Manuel Soto’s direction, Blue Beetle is a superhero movie that sets itself apart within the bloated genre through the deeply connected bonds of Jaime and the Reyes family.
reviews.author: Alyssa Mora

reviews.text: It's lighter, more fun, and delivers the jokes, bright colors and nods to ridiculousness that you want from a superhero movie. And speaking of the superhero, the Blue Beetle emerges as relatable and easy to cheer for.
reviews.author: Kaely Monahan

reviews.text: Blue Beetle never loses sight of the community it seeks to honor, not once pandering nor offering surface-level representation of what it means to be Latino.
reviews.author: Yolanda Machado

reviews.text: A strong cast led by Xolo Maridueña pushes this unessential superhero entry into the win column
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: An origin story, and one that climaxes with two computer-generated characters whomping the tar out of each other, but the movie avoids feeling like yet another by-the-numbers superhero tale.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: There’s a perkiness that’s hard to resist and a base-level competency that’s hard not to appreciate, a small beam of blue light in an otherwise dark time for superheroes.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: The movie seems to genuinely like these characters – and, moreover, the characters seem to genuinely like each other, lending Blue Beetle some real warmth amidst the standard business of super-suited enemies smashing into each other.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: For a film that incessantly natters on about Jaime’s purpose, “Blue Beetle” has bafflingly little sense of what its own might be.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Xolo Maridueña’s breakthrough performance and solid family dynamics elevate the otherwise typical superhero origin story.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Give it a few more drafts and "Blue Beetle" may have emerged as something extraordinary.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: It's a minor miracle that this film survived the leap from "throwaway streaming vehicle" to "bonafide blockbuster release."
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: A bug worth catching.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: A self-contained and smartly crafted film that ranks among the DCEU’s very best. Even though, admittedly, that doesn’t say nearly as much as it ought to.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Overall, this is an amusing superhero movie that offers many crowd-pleasing moments. It does not stand out above the rest as anything special, but it delivers the action, family, and fun you will expect.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: Arguably the most derivative offering the tired genre has yet to offer, borrowing elements from so many forebearers that it plays like a conventional pastiche.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Blue Beetle might not be a unique take on the superhero origin story, but Soto and Dunnet-Alcocer do prove that a smaller scale, lighter approach within the DC Universe can work.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: A great time at the movies. A fantastic introduction to Jaime Reyes, and a love letter to the Latino culture - focusing on family as its foundation. A win for longtime fans of the superhero, and for the future of the new DCU. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The brisk, cheeky, unabashed gizmo-happy triviality of “Blue Beetle,” a superhero origin story from the DC side of the tracks, is enough to make the film feel like a breath of fresh pulp.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: It’s the kind of thing we’ve all seen way too many times before and felt extra disappointing here because there’s a lot in this movie that does feel unique, but then it feels squandered.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: One wishes more were done to separate it from the pack outside of its specific setting, but it manages to be just enough in many places to be entertaining.
reviews.author: Josh Parham

reviews.text:
Fun, vibrant and at times emotional family adventure that injects an authentic flavor and identity into the usual superhero origin story. Xolo Maridueña is a young movie star!
[Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Filled with comedy, heart, family values, action, and lovable characters, there is something in this movie for everyone. We can only hope that Jaime sticks around after the DC reboot.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Maridueña brings warmth, charisma, and sincerity to Jaime and it is expressed in the way he cares about making his family proud and getting them out of their situation.
reviews.author: Catherine Gonzales

reviews.text: Blue Beetle should win audiences over by leaning heavily on the humor and heart, but also offering the type of quality VFX-laden action that comic book movie enthusiasts have come to expect.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: It has more heart and humor than most in this well worn genre. That ought to count for something.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Ángel Manuel Soto’s Blue Beetle is the cinematic VICKS Bibaporrú for the DCU! Oozing Latin pride and authenticity, Blue Beetle is an inspiring and heartfelt journey that embraces its Latin American roots while forgoing the universe-building entanglements.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: "Blue Beetle" feels like a welcomed throwback, an old school superhero movie spiced with Latin flavors, retro vibes, and a warm, affectionate family at its core. You've seen origin stories before, but never one made and told from this particular POV.
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

synopsis: Recent college grad Jaime Reyes returns home full of aspirations for his future, only to find that home is not quite as he left it. As he searches to find his purpose in the world, fate intervenes when Jaime unexpectedly finds himself in possession of an ancient relic of alien biotechnology: the Scarab. When the Scarab suddenly chooses Jaime to be its symbiotic host, he is bestowed with an incredible suit of armor capable of extraordinary and unpredictable powers, forever changing his destiny as he becomes the Super Hero BLUE BEETLE.
